definition.def: If you accompany someone, you go somewhere with them. [formal]
examples: Ken agreed to accompany me on a trip to Africa. [VERB noun]
She was accompanied by her younger brother. [VERB noun]
The Prime Minister, accompanied by the governor, led the President up to the house. [VERB-ed]

definition.def: If one thing accompanies another, it happens or exists at the same time, or as a result of it. [formal]
examples: This volume of essays was designed to accompany an exhibition in Cologne. [VERB noun]
The proposal was instantly voted through, accompanied by enthusiastic applause. [VERB-ed]
Perhaps the accompanying illustration will explain it. [VERB-ing]

definition.def: If you accompany a singer or a musician, you play one part of a piece of music while they sing or play the main tune.
examples: He sang and Alice accompanied him on the piano. [VERB noun]
She was accompanied on the guitar by her brother Massimo. [VERB-ed]
